project: Learning When to Recheck: Cost-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Navigation with Stale Maps
source_policy: Primary papers and author/publisher records; PDFs available without a paywall at verification time. Local PDFs are not redistributed in Git.
scope: Ten-paper curated set, not an exhaustive novelty review. Nine proposal references plus the close CTP-with-sensing predecessor.

papers.title: Canadian Traveler Problem with Remote Sensing
papers.finding: Defines travel-plus-sensing cost and implements EXP and sampled single-step value-of-information policies within FSSN.
papers.evidence: Sections 4 and 5.2, PDF pages 4-5; printed pages 440-441.
papers.adaptation: Reimplement the sampled single-step VOI idea with physical travel to visible inspection viewpoints, persistent beliefs, noisy observations, and task budgets.
papers.mismatch: Original sense(v,e) is a remote query; travel-dependent sensing cost is not the same as moving the agent to inspect. The single-trip independent-edge setting differs from persistent task sequences.
papers.reuse: Algorithmic adaptation with attribution; no author-maintained code was located in the bounded search. Do not claim exact reproduction.
papers.review_depth: Primary-source metadata, abstract, and targeted relevant full-paper sections; not an exhaustive reproduction audit

papers.title: D* Lite
papers.role: Reactive replanning foundation, not an inspection policy
papers.finding: Reuses search information for efficient replanning as traversability information changes.
papers.evidence: Author abstract and erratum; paper algorithm and experiments.
papers.adaptation: Use a shared simple shortest-path implementation first. D* Lite is an optional later optimization, not the name of a Dijkstra implementation.
papers.mismatch: Receiving updated edge costs does not decide whether obtaining those observations is worth a physical inspection.
papers.reuse: Cite conceptual replanning relationship. If implementing D* Lite later, follow author pseudocode and erratum.
papers.review_depth: Primary-source metadata, abstract, and targeted relevant full-paper sections; not an exhaustive reproduction audit

papers.title: FreMEn: Frequency Map Enhancement for Long-Term Mobile Robot Autonomy in Changing Environments
papers.role: Temporal predictor control when periodic schedules are evaluated
papers.finding: Models periodic environmental changes spectrally and combines periodic prediction with recent-state persistence.
papers.evidence: Sections III.D (PDF page 5) and navigation experiments; DOI 10.1109/TRO.2017.2665664.
papers.adaptation: Use a predictor with the same planner/inspection rule and fit it only on shared training observations. Compare on periodic and nonperiodic scenarios.
papers.mismatch: State prediction and inspection selection are separate components. An exponential decay model alone is not FreMEn.
papers.reuse: Audit official implementation licensing before reuse. A lightweight approximation must be called FreMEn-inspired, not a reproduction.
papers.review_depth: Primary-source metadata, abstract, and targeted relevant full-paper sections; not an exhaustive reproduction audit

papers.title: GOAT-Bench: A Benchmark for Multi-Modal Lifelong Navigation
papers.finding: Evaluates navigation sequences with multiple goal modalities and compares implicit and explicit memory.
papers.evidence: Abstract; task formulation and memory analysis.
papers.adaptation: Borrow the rationale for cross-task evaluation, not benchmark scores or full multimodal agents.
papers.mismatch: Multimodal object-goal navigation differs from known-layout point-goal navigation with changing passages.
papers.reuse: Related work and protocol inspiration; no direct performance comparison without task matching.
papers.review_depth: Primary-source metadata, abstract, and targeted relevant full-paper sections; not an exhaustive reproduction audit

papers.title: MemoNav: Working Memory Model for Visual Navigation
papers.finding: Combines short-term and long-term representations with selective forgetting and graph attention for image-goal navigation.
papers.adaptation: Explain why relevance and physical validity are distinct; age and route consequence features address a different question.
papers.mismatch: Forgetting low-relevance visual features is not physically checking whether a still-relevant passage is blocked.
papers.reuse: Related work; avoid porting the full visual navigation stack for the mid-project deadline.
papers.review_depth: Primary-source metadata, abstract, and targeted relevant full-paper sections; not an exhaustive reproduction audit

papers.title: 3D-Mem: 3D Scene Memory for Embodied Exploration and Reasoning
papers.finding: Uses multi-view Memory Snapshots and Frontier Snapshots to combine known scene information with exploration opportunities.
papers.adaptation: Use to distinguish exploring unknown space from revisiting known-but-stale route state.
papers.mismatch: Visual scene reasoning and exploration are not a matched low-dimensional passage-state benchmark.
papers.reuse: Related work only for the first implementation.
papers.review_depth: Primary-source metadata, abstract, and targeted relevant full-paper sections; not an exhaustive reproduction audit

papers.title: EvoNav-Bench: Benchmarking Lifelong Navigation in Evolving Environments
papers.role: Closest contemporary benchmark motivation and heuristic controls
papers.finding: Changes object locations between tasks and tests Frontier-Update, Fail-then-Update, and Stage-Reset strategies.
papers.evidence: Sections 3-4; Appendix A, PDF page 14, explicitly distinguishes local object-layout changes from room-topology changes.
papers.adaptation: Adapt reactive correction and memory-reset ideas to passage beliefs and cross-task evaluation.
papers.mismatch: Preserves room topology and overall navigability; our passage interventions change which routes are traversable while retaining goal reachability.
papers.reuse: Related work and adapted controls, not benchmark reproduction or imported benchmark scores.
papers.review_depth: Primary-source metadata, abstract, and targeted relevant full-paper sections; not an exhaustive reproduction audit

papers.title: SPIN: Simultaneous Perception Interaction and Navigation
papers.role: Evidence that learning when/what to observe is established
papers.finding: Coordinates active visual perception with whole-body mobile manipulation and navigation.
papers.evidence: Abstract and method; PPO training discussion on PDF page 4.
papers.adaptation: Use as active-perception precedent and contrast with high-level inspection decisions over stale memory.
papers.mismatch: Whole-body manipulation, ego-vision, and continuous control differ from our fixed low-level navigation controller.
papers.reuse: Related work; no claim that our PPO architecture reproduces SPIN.
papers.review_depth: Primary-source metadata, abstract, and targeted relevant full-paper sections; not an exhaustive reproduction audit

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning for Active Perception in Autonomous Navigation
papers.venue: arXiv:2602.01266v1; arXiv record reports ICRA 2026 acceptance
papers.publication_status: author-reported conference acceptance; accessible preprint inspected
papers.role: Modern active-sensing RL comparator in related work
papers.finding: Learns aerial motion and actuated camera control with local depth/geometry observations and an information-related reward.
papers.evidence: Sections II-III and paper introduction; code link in PDF page 2.
papers.adaptation: Use to motivate sensing as a decision and explain differences in observation/action spaces.
papers.mismatch: Aerial low-level control and camera actuation do not provide a drop-in stale-passage baseline.
papers.reuse: Study method and evaluation; avoid adopting a full aerial simulator stack.
papers.review_depth: Primary-source metadata, abstract, and targeted relevant full-paper sections; not an exhaustive reproduction audit

papers.title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
papers.theme: RL optimizer and matched algorithmic control
papers.role: Shared optimizer for proposed policy and matched RL baseline
papers.finding: Defines a clipped policy objective and actor-critic optimization using repeated minibatch updates.
papers.adaptation: Use the same optimizer, network capacity, training budget and seeds for proposed and ablated observations.
papers.mismatch: PPO is an optimizer, not the project novelty. Standard per-step GAE does not automatically handle variable-duration decisions.
papers.reuse: Prefer a maintained, license-verified implementation; resolve semi-Markov discounting before reporting experiments.
papers.review_depth: Primary-source metadata, abstract, and targeted relevant full-paper sections; not an exhaustive reproduction audit
